pharm: Gastric acid secretion inhibitor / antisecretory agent
quick: 20-40 mg PO once daily; IV 20-40 mg/day
Use only if clearly needed; limited data
No adjustment; caution in severe impairment
No direct interaction; may worsen symptoms
Mg, B12 on long-term use; symptom response
summary: Esomeprazole is the S-isomer of omeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor that produces durable suppression of gastric acid by irreversibly inhibiting the H+/K+ ATPase. Used for GERD, erosive esophagitis healing, peptic ulcer, H. pylori eradication and pathological hypersecretory states. Typical adult dose 20-40 mg once daily before a meal. Long-term use is associated with hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency and increased fracture risk.
indications: Healing and maintenance of erosive esophagitis
Risk reduction of NSAID-associated gastric ulcer
Helicobacter pylori eradication (in combination with antibiotics)
Pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
Prevention of rebleeding of gastric/duodenal ulcers after endoscopic therapy (IV)

dosage.d: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks; may extend to 8 weeks
40 mg once daily with amoxicillin 1 g BID and clarithromycin 500 mg BID x 10 days
20-40 mg once daily up to 6 months
40 mg twice daily; titrate to acid output

admin: Swallow capsule whole at least 1 hour before a meal, preferably in the morning
If unable to swallow, open capsule and mix granules in soft food (applesauce) without chewing
For NG/oral suspension, mix granules in water and administer without crushing the enteric coating
IV: administer over 3 minutes (push) or 10-30 minutes (infusion); flush line before and after
Do not crush or chew the enteric-coated granules
moa: Esomeprazole is a substituted benzimidazole that accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculus of the gastric parietal cell, where it is converted to the active sulfenamide. This irreversibly binds the H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump), the terminal step of acid secretion, producing dose-dependent and prolonged inhibition of both basal and stimulated gastric acid output. As the S-enantiomer of omeprazole it undergoes less first-pass metabolism, giving higher systemic exposure.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to esomeprazole, other benzimidazole PPIs, or formulation components
relative: Risk of osteoporotic fracture with long-term high-dose use
Hypomagnesemia or use of other Mg-lowering drugs

preg: Available data do not show a clear drug-associated risk of major birth defects. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; epidemiologic data on omeprazole are largely reassuring.
lact: Esomeprazole/omeprazole is present in human milk in small amounts. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in renal impairment; esomeprazole is metabolized hepatically and renal clearance of unchanged drug is minimal. Use caution in severe renal impairment as experience is limited.
hepatic: No adjustment in mild to moderate impairment. In severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) systemic exposure is increased; do not exceed 20 mg daily.

major: Clopidogrel - may reduce active metabolite and antiplatelet effect
moderate: Digoxin - increased absorption with raised gastric pH
Drugs needing gastric acidity (ketoconazole, itraconazole, iron salts) - reduced absorption
interactions.food: Food reduces and delays absorption; take at least 1 hour before eating.
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacokinetic interaction; alcohol may aggravate reflux symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive chromogranin A elevation; can interfere with secretin stimulation testing for gastrinoma.

monitoring: Symptom response; reassess need for continued therapy periodically
Serum magnesium before and during prolonged therapy, especially with digoxin or diuretics
Vitamin B12 with long-term use (>=2-3 years)
Renal function if signs of interstitial nephritis (rash, fever, eosinophilia)
counsel: Take at least 1 hour before a meal, preferably in the morning
Swallow capsules whole; do not crush or chew
Report persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, tremor, palpitations or seizures
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration needed
Tell your doctor about long-term use if you have osteoporosis risk
pk: Acid suppression within 1 hour; full effect over days
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture
pearls: S-isomer of omeprazole with higher and more consistent exposure than racemic omeprazole
Effect is cumulative over 3-5 days due to irreversible pump inhibition
Reassess at 8 weeks; avoid indefinite use without indication
Stopping abruptly after prolonged use can cause rebound acid hypersecretion
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Reported overdoses are largely without serious sequelae; symptoms may include drowsiness, blurred vision, confusion, tachycardia and GI upset. There is no specific antidote; esomeprazole is highly protein bound and not effectively dialyzed. Treat symptomatically and supportively.
